_readme: Small rules database. 'items' says what the detector looks for; 'regions' says where each item goes. A region only lists what differs from 'default'. The regional profiles are illustrative starting points: confirm them against your own municipality's published list before relying on them.

Flatten it, remove tape and plastic, and keep it dry.

contaminated.tip: Grease ruins paper recycling. Tear off any clean part to recycle; the soiled part is general waste.

clean.tip: Keep it dry and flat. No need to remove staples.

contaminated.tip: Food-soiled paper cannot be recycled. Put it in general waste.

clean.tip: Most disposable cups have a plastic lining that paper mills reject. Empty the liquid first.

contaminated.tip: Scrape and rinse it and it becomes recyclable. If it will not come clean, general waste.

clean.tip: Film jams sorting machines. Use a store drop-off point if one exists, otherwise general waste.
Multi-layer plastic and foil cannot be separated for recycling.
Remove any sticker or packaging first.

clean.tip: Flatten it and keep it dry so the kabadiwala or MRF can take it.

contaminated.tip: Scrape leftover food into wet waste. The greasy board goes with dry waste as non-recyclable.

clean.tip: Keep it dry and bundle it.

contaminated.tip: Food-soiled paper and tissue is usually taken with wet waste. Check your local body's list.
Empty the food into wet waste and rinse. Unrinsed, it spoils the rest of the dry waste.

clean.tip: Keep it clean and dry with dry waste.
Multi-layer plastic goes with dry waste, never wet.
Empty the liquid, then dry waste.
